title: The last real programmers are dying out...
body_text: The programmer, 4 years ago, science classified 10 known variants of this animal, and the taxonomy held up pretty well until an asteroid hit in 2023 and nearly wiped them off the earth. But since then, the habitat has changed. And nine out of 10 developers are now using AI to write their code, which means the one who doesn't is now endangered. Meanwhile, several new species have emerged recently, and in order to understand them, we need stereotypes, which experts still estimate are about 99% accurate about 12% of the time. In today's video, we'll look at the seven programmer stereotypes of 2026 to help you find out which one you've mutated into. But first up, we have the non-technical vibe coder. This specimen doesn't know what a for loop is, and he doesn't really care. He describes himself as a founder, and his entire tech stack is a chat window with a prompt that says, "It's still not working." He launches a SaaS on Tuesday, it gets hacked on Wednesday because the API keys are hardcoded on the front end, and on Thursday, he posts a thread about resilience. His natural predator is Edsger Dijkstra, and his natural habitat is a screenshot of monthly recurring revenue that was also generated by AI because he doesn't know how to use dev tools. Evolutionary biologists have traced his lineage directly back to the boot camp programmer who normalized not understanding computer science fundamentals. Next, the closest living relative to the non-technical vibe coder is the prompt casino degenerate. This guy is technical, but only if it's easier than LeetCode medium. He pulls the lever, the agent spins, and about 60% of the time, he gets a tasty piece of cheese he can make a PR out of. He spends $400 per month of his own money on coding agents because his company just set a $29 per month employee limit after agentic abuse. When the code is good, it's because he's a prompt engineer, and when it's bad, it's because Opus is nerfed. His family left him after he cashed out the kids' 529 college plans to give his agent full API access to his Calcy account. But that's okay because the latency with local voice models is low enough that it feels real. Next, the apex predator of the prompt casino degenerate, the Swarm Lord, who biologists classify as eusocial. This guy knows how to code and enjoy it, but he's gaslit himself into thinking he's never been more productive. He runs 12 agents in parallel from his phone, and his favorite thing to do while his agents work is tell you that he runs 12 agents in parallel from his phone. He hasn't looked at a line of code in years, but he has strong opinions about which model has the best taste. His natural predator is uptime, and his mating call is saying that writing software is a solved problem. The Swarm Lord feasts on our next variant, the Slop Maintainer. This guy wrote a date formatting library in 2019 that now has 40 million weekly downloads and is critical web infrastructure. He gets hundreds of PRs per month that are each co-authored by Claude, and in October he gets 10,000 more from junior devs in Bangalore hoping to get a free t-shirt. He survives on the $95 he gets from his GitHub sponsors every month while he watches the famous library maintainers make millions getting acquired by Shopify. His natural predator is a North Korean maintainer offering to help, and his mating call is threatening to archive the repo every other month. The maintainer never found out who sent those 10,000 PRs, but the biologists have, and they're calling him the unemployed junior. His whole life he did everything right, good grades, studied leetcode, didn't kiss any girls, and he's been rejected by every AI screener that's come across his resume. He graduated in 2024, which was about 6 months after the last entry-level job on Earth was filled. His GitHub contribution graph is a solid wall of green made entirely of readme typo fixes and Python projects from school. His natural habitat is a Discord server, and his natural predator is the non-technical vibe coder who can build everything he can with just with a marketing degree. His mating call is asking if anybody is hiring, and the guy who keeps saying no is our next specimen, the old jaded developer. This guy is in his mid-30s. He learned grunt, then gulp, then webpack. He got excited for jQuery, then Angular, then React. He even stuck around for hooks and Next.js, but now he's old, tired, and couldn't care less about benchmarks. He's not going to learn your harness, he's not going to read your system prompt, and he's not going to run 12 of anything. The full extent of his AI usage is hitting tab in GitHub Copilot, which he's gotten for free since 2023 because he contributed to Gatsby back in the day. He doesn't know there's a chat window in his IDE, he misses 100 seconds videos, and when Copilot suggests something wrong, he just deletes it by hand like a monk raking gravel. He's not anti-AI, he just has a parent-teacher conference at 4:00 p.m. and is coaching his third grader's basketball at 7:00. But, you know who is anti-AI? Our final specimen, the purest. This man is the best in us, he's noble, brave, handsome, and has 20 years of experience in a world that no longer exists. He hasn't had a job since MCP was released, which by the way, he thinks is just Corba with worse security. When he did have a job, he wrote every line by hand and would gladly tell you the big O of any slop you whipped up. His favorite books are Introduction to Algorithms and The Pragmatic Programmer. And nowadays, he can be found in his natural habitat on Hacker News talking about the craft of writing software. Biologists estimate that there are fewer than 10,000 of these left in the wild, and their numbers are dwindling by the day.
